1. Investment view: what the price is paying for
HUL is a very good business trading as if its recent operating wobble were behind it. The debate is not about quality (market leader
in categories that make over 90% of turnover, negative working capital, ~24% ROIC, ~90% payout). It is about how much the next
decade of cash flow is worth when the risk-free rate is 7.3%.
Reverse DCF: what must happen at today's price
Reading: at a 9% discount rate the price is simply our base case (7.9% revenue
CAGR, 23.5% margin). At 10% it needs ~11% revenue growth for ten years,
against 5% in FY26 and 12% in H1 FY27. CAPM gives 9.1% with the raw beta
of 0.33 and 10.7% with the 2-year regression beta of 0.62 (G-sec 7.3%, ERP
5.5%). We use 10%, the midpoint; the whole call is sensitive to this one

Management and several brokers describe demand as stable with rural and urban in step; premium products are
outgrowing mass (Macquarie, Morgan Stanley, Jul-26). The GST cut of Sep-25 disrupted trade in Q2 FY26 (a soft base for Q2 FY27)
and lifted volumes from Q3 FY26 (a harder base from Q3 FY27).
We found no hard market-share data for this report. Qualitatively, the threats are regional and D2C brands in
beauty and nutrition (which HUL answered with Minimalist and OZiva), private labels and quick-commerce-native assortments.
HUL's response is portfolio and channel transformation, funded by 3%-of-sales capex.
HUL says it will "calibrate" price pass-through to protect the franchise and expects only low-single-digit price
increases through the year, so margin protection relies on cost savings and mix, not price.
